reference.title: Sled 45 degrees One Leg Press
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the plate comes toward you, breathe out as you press it away.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s toward you, a short pause, about 1.2 s press

prescription.tempo: 2-0-1-0 (2 s down, no pause, 1 s up)
prescription.load: Machine load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can move through the full range shown with good form, leaving about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Add a small amount of load when every rep of every set reaches the full range with good form.

cues.text: Sit with the hips and back flat on the pads and hold the side handles. Right foot in the middle of the plate, toes out a little; the left foot rests on the floor. Press the plate out to nearly straight leg and turn the safety catches out.
Breathe in and let the plate come toward you under control, the knee tracking over the toes.
Stop when the knee is bent about 90 degrees, before the lower back starts to curl off the pad.
Breathe out and press the plate away through the whole foot, heel down.
Leg nearly straight, knees soft; go again. Do all reps, then switch legs.

mistakes.mistake: Lower back and hips curling off the pad at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Stop the plate a little earlier, or set the seat further back.
Place the foot a little higher and press through the heel and mid-foot.

mistakes.mistake: Locking the knees hard at the top
mistakes.fix: Stop just short of a hard lockout.
Keep the knee in line with the second toe; use a lighter load.

kinematics.norm: From nearly straight to about 90 degrees; knee forces rise with knee flexion in the leg press (Escamilla 1998)
Hips flex deeply at the bottom while the pelvis stays on the seat (common coaching)
Heel stays down on the plate; the ankle bends with the knee (common coaching)
Hips and back stay on the pads through the rep (machine design)
Middle of the plate, about hip width; higher feet bring in more hip, lower feet more knee (common coaching)
Controlled, about 2 s toward you and 1-1.5 s press (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Sled 45 degrees One Leg Press, video (movement reference)
Escamilla et al. 1998, biomechanics of the knee during closed kinetic chain and open kinetic chain exercises (Med Sci Sports Exerc 30(4):556-569; PubMed 9565938)

cautions: Turn the safety catches back in before getting out of the sled, and never let the plate come down past them.
Keep the lower back on the pad; stop the descent where the hips start to curl.
Knee pain: shorten the range or move the foot higher on the plate.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee pain: press through a pain-free range.
Low-back discomfort: shorten the range so the pelvis stays on the seat.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Prime mover: straightens the knee; open-chain extension works the quadriceps hardest near straight legs (Escamilla et al. 1998).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extends the hip from the deep hip bend at the bottom (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus helps extend the hip from deep flexion (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Lengthen at the top with the knee straight; they do not lift the load.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Keep the ankle steady against the plate.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the working knee in line with the foot.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the pelvis still on the seat.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the side handles to keep the hips down.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the side handles to keep the hips down.

guides.label: Knee about 90 degrees at the bottom
